R1873.summary: A duplicate despatch of Alvise Mocenigo, Venetian ambassador in Rome (the later Doge Alvise I), to Doge Lorenzo Priuli: the four cipher passages tell how Paul IV's face changed when Mocenigo raised the matter, and concern the Carafa nephews and the bishopric of Brescia; Mocenigo fears the Carafa will keep the Pope from hearing him soon. Read by Paolo Bonavoglia (crittologia.eu).
R1873.en:
His Holiness, when I began to speak of this, I saw change somewhat in his face and in his eyes, [answering], to tell
the truth, rather coldly; so I hope for no good office at all from His Lordship, and this because it is common talk
that he will do everything, as I have written at other times, to have the bishopric of Brescia; the will of the most
illustrious Carafa will prevail. So I remain with the suspicion that these lords Carafa, his nephews, because of these
bishoprics, are not pleased that I should be heard so soon by His Holiness on his account.

system: Venetian nomenclator, each sign a base letter with a superscript letter (a^n, c^a ...), standing for letters, syllables and words; Bonavoglia puts it in the 'Cifra n. 3' family (1577), similar to the cipher Michel Surian used in England in 1557.
